headline: Google has launched Deep Review, an AI tool that checks research papers for maths errors, logical gaps and unsupported claims.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a public launch with stated limits, but the accuracy figures are Google's own.
summary: R&D World reports that Google Research released Deep Review on 14 Oct 2026, after pilots that gave feedback on more than 15,000 manuscripts; AI agents examine each section of a document and a final agent checks claims against Google Search to catch invented material. In a June preprint an earlier version found 89.7 percent of known errors in a small test of 29 errors, but pilot users also saw it wrongly challenge correct proofs, so researchers still have to check its comments.
importance_line: Researchers and journal reviewers may get help checking a growing flow of AI-assisted papers, but the accuracy figures are Google's own and rest on a small test.
